Assam tops NATGRID use, new criminal laws implementation ranking
Guwahati: Assam has emerged as a frontrunner in intelligence-led policing following the implementation of India’s new criminal justice laws, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said.
The state topped the country in the use of National Intelligence Grid (NATGRID) and recorded a compliance score significantly higher than the national average in implementing the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).
Gandiva and Sudarshan platforms in Sept 2026, the highest in the country, Sarma said in a post on X.
“Ranking No. 1 in NATGRID usage nationwide in September 2026, with 2,37,121 activities across Gandiva and Sudarshan platforms, Assam is strengthening its ability to access and utilise intelligence inputs for more effective law enforcement and internal security,” he added.
NATGRID is Centre’s intelligence-sharing platform that lets authorised agencies access and analyse data from multiple databases. Gandiva and Sudarshan are among its key tools, used for identity matching, data queries and investigation support.
The ranking follows Assam’s strong showing in rolling out the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), which replaced the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act on July 1, 2024.
Sarma shared the ranking list from New Criminal Laws Implementation dashboard of MHA, which shows Assam at the top of the latest ranking of states and union territories, scoring 95.75 and edging out Haryana.
Haryana came second with 95.27, followed by Chandigarh (92.82), Andaman and Nicobar Islands (92.15) and Goa (91.76). Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu ranked sixth with 90.47, ahead of Maharashtra (89.56) and Rajasthan (89.43) in seventh and eighth places.
“When it comes to fighting crime, Assam means business. Our policing is focused on stronger enforcement, swift action and protecting every citizen. Assam ranks No. 1 in the implementation of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, as per the @HMOIndia NCLI dashboard,” Sarma wrote on X.
He added, “May Maa Durga bless us with the courage to fight crime, uphold justice and protect every citizen.”
